title: The $6-ε$ Expansion for Long-Range Lee--Yang and Percolation Criticality
authors: Zhiyi Li, Kun Chen, Zhijie Fan, Youjin Deng
abstract: The crossover from long-range (LR) to short-range (SR) criticality in percolation has remained unsettled because previous renormalization-group (RG) analysis within the $ε'=3σ-d$ expansion fixes the anomalous dimension at $η=2-σ$, whereas SR percolation has $η_{\rm SR}<0$ near $d=6$. Sak's matching condition then places the crossover above $σ=2$, outside the regime in which the LR interaction dominates. In spatial dimension $d=6-ε$, we formulate a perturbative expansion for the LR $φ^3$ field theory and perform a one-loop RG analysis throughout the perturbatively accessible nonclassical regime $0<δ<ε/3$, where $δ= 2-σ$. We derive the one-loop corrections to the critical exponents $η$ and $ν$, which acquire nontrivial dependence on $ε$ and $δ$. They reduce to their mean-field values at the LR upper critical line and continuously recover the SR $6-ε$ results as $σ\to2$. These results support a crossover threshold $σ_*=2$ and remove the apparent discontinuity of $η$ between the LR and SR values within this framework. The same approach also yields the anomalous and edge exponents of the LR Lee--Yang universality class and $q$-state Potts universality classes with $q<2$.
summary: This paper uses a $d=6-\epsilon$ renormalization group expansion on an effective $\phi^3$ field theory to study critical phenomena in percolation with long-range interactions. The authors successfully derive one-loop corrections for the critical exponents, demonstrating that the crossover between long-range and short-range universality classes occurs smoothly at $\sigma^*=2$. This resolves previous theoretical conflicts regarding the nature of this transition.
main_problem: The paper addresses the long-standing theoretical problem of determining the crossover behavior between long-range (LR) and short-range (SR) criticality in percolation systems.
main_result: The authors derive one-loop RG corrections showing that the critical exponents vary continuously across the crossover threshold at $\sigma^*=2$, resolving apparent discontinuities found in previous analyses.
method: They employ a perturbative Renormalization Group (RG) analysis using a $d = 6 - \epsilon$ expansion applied to an effective $\phi^3$ field theory.
model_or_system: The study models the critical behavior of percolation and Lee-Yang singularities using an $n$-component $\phi^3$ field theory, incorporating long-range interactions characterized by a power-law decay $J(r) \sim r^{-(d+\sigma)}$.
key_observables:
Critical exponents such as the anomalous dimension ($\eta$) and correlation-length exponent ($
u$).
important_parameters: The interaction range parameter $\sigma$, the spatial dimension $d$ (analyzed via $\epsilon$), and the crossover threshold $\sigma^*=2$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is perturbative, valid for small $\epsilon$ and within a specific nonclassical regime ($0 < \delta < \epsilon/3$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the universality-class diagram in the $(\sigma, d)$ plane, comparing various theoretical predictions for the crossover region.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the field-theoretic framework using an effective action involving $\phi^3$ terms. It then performs a one-loop RG analysis by calculating counterterms and deriving beta functions to determine the fixed points and exponents in the LR expansion, finally showing continuity across the SR limit.
why_interesting: While focused on classical critical phenomena, the rigorous application of advanced field theory techniques (RG flow) to establish universal crossover behavior is a cornerstone technique applicable to quantum phase transitions in many-body systems.
